page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance powered by 64-bit Arm architecture AWS Graviton processors. It features 96 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, with a single execution thread per core, resulting in 96 vCPUs. The hardware configuration integrates 768.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

As a bare-metal system without hypervisor virtualization overhead, the instance provides direct access to physical CPU and memory resources. The server does not bundle discrete graphics hardware or local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for persistent data management. Network interface capability is defined by a 200 Gbps baseline bandwidth specification, enabling high-throughput communication across distributed infrastructure.

From an architectural perspective, the 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides dense capacity for applications bounded by RAM volume rather than storage IOPS. Because storage must be provisioned externally, operational cost efficiency is influenced by external disk dependencies alongside bare-metal resource consumption. The instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, memory-heavy analytics pipelines, and enterprise data processing.
